🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Use prepositions of place (in, on, under, behind...) correctly.
- Say exactly where a person or an object is.
- Combine prepositions with "there is / there are" and the verb "to be".
- Describe the position of things in a room or a picture.

🔍 Warm-up
Look at your pen right now. Is it ON the desk? IN your bag? UNDER a book? These little words (on, in, under) are prepositions of place, and this lesson makes them easy.

I. The main prepositions of place

<rect x="270" y="40" width="140" height="34" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="340" y="62" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Where...?</text>
<g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1" opacity="0.6">
<line x1="340" y1="74" x2="90" y2="110"/>
<line x1="340" y1="74" x2="240" y2="110"/>

<line x1="340" y1="74" x2="590" y2="110"/>
</g>
<g font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">
<text x="90" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold" fill="#16a34a">Inside/on</text>
<text x="90" y="125" text-anchor="middle">in · on · under</text>
<text x="240" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold" fill="#e11d48">Front/back</text>
<text x="240" y="125" text-anchor="middle">behind · in front of</text>

<text x="440" y="125" text-anchor="middle">next to · between · near</text>

<text x="340" y="263" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">The cat is under the table.</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📘 Rule (vocabulary)
Prepositions of place tell us WHERE something is. The most common are:
- in = inside something (in the box, in the room).
- on = on a surface, touching the top (on the table, on the wall).
- under = below something (under the bed).
- behind = at the back of (behind the door).
- in front of = at the front of (in front of the school).
- next to / beside = at the side of (next to the window).
- between = in the middle of two things (between the two chairs).
- near = close to (near the station).
- opposite = facing (opposite the bank).
- above = higher than (above the shelf).
- below = lower than (below the picture).

📏 Form
The preposition comes BEFORE the place noun:
subject + verb + preposition + the + place.
- The cat is under the table.
- There is a lamp on the desk.

II. In, on, under — the three basics

[[FIG]]<svg viewBox="0 0 660 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="330" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">A Room Scene</text>
<rect x="50" y="60" width="560" height="170" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<rect x="380" y="150" width="140" height="60" rx="4" fill="#3b82f6" opacity="0.25" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="1.5"/>

<rect x="120" y="185" width="70" height="45" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="155" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">table</text>
<circle cx="155" cy="222" r="6" fill="#e11d48"/>
<text x="155" y="245" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="currentColor" font-weight="bold">cat — under the table</text>
<rect x="230" y="75" width="60" height="40" fill="#3b82f6" opacity="0.3"/>
<text x="260" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="currentColor" font-weight="bold">poster — on the wall</text>
<rect x="500" y="80" width="45" height="60" fill="none" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>

</svg>[[/FIG]]
✏️ Worked examples
- The keys are in the drawer.
- The book is on the shelf.
- The ball is under the chair.
- My shoes are in the box.
- There is a poster on the wall.

🛠️ Method: choosing in / on / under
Step 1 — Is the object INSIDE something closed or bordered? → in.
Step 2 — Is it TOUCHING the top of a surface? → on.
Step 3 — Is it BELOW something? → under.

👀 Note
We say "on the wall" and "on the ceiling" even though they are vertical or above us, because the object touches that surface. We also say "on the left / on the right / in the middle".

III. Position words for describing a scene
📏 Form (there is / there are + preposition)
- There is a bag next to the door.
- There are two pictures above the bed.
- The school is opposite the mosque.
- The bank is between the café and the shop.

✏️ Worked description
There is a big desk in the middle of my bedroom. On the desk there is a computer and some books. Next to the desk there is a chair. Behind the door there is a mirror. Under the bed there are two boxes. In front of the window there are some green plants.

⚠️ Common mistakes
- in / on confusion: The picture is in the wall → on the wall.
- Forgetting "of": in front the house → in front of the house.
- "between" needs TWO things: between the door → between the door and the window.
- next / next to: The bank is next the shop → next to the shop.

IV. Asking and answering about position

[[FIG]]<svg viewBox="0 0 660 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="330" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Asking "Where?"</text>
<rect x="30" y="50" width="150" height="36" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="105" y="73" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Where</text>
<rect x="195" y="50" width="150" height="36" rx="8" fill="#16a34a"/>
<text x="270" y="73" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">is / are</text>
<rect x="360" y="50" width="150" height="36" rx="8" fill="#e11d48"/>
<text x="435" y="73" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">subject ?</text>
<line x1="180" y1="68" x2="195" y2="68" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
<line x1="345" y1="68" x2="360" y2="68" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="60" y="105" width="540" height="90" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
<text x="330" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" font-weight="bold">Examples</text>
<text x="330" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">Where is my phone? — It's on the table.</text>
<text x="330" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">Where are the children? — They are in the garden.</text>
<text x="330" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">is = singular subject · are = plural subject</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📏 Form (questions with "Where")
Where + is/are + subject ?
- Where is my phone? — It's on the table.
- Where are the children? — They are in the garden.

🛠️ Method: answering a "Where" question
Step 1 — Use the verb "to be" (is / are).
Step 2 — Add the correct preposition.
Step 3 — Add the place.
Example: Where is the cat? — It is under the sofa.

👀 Note
Prepositions of place also work for towns and directions:
- The pharmacy is next to the school.
- Turn left. The park is on your right.
- Go straight on. The station is opposite the hotel.

✏️ Worked dialogue
- Excuse me, where is the post office?
- It's next to the bank, opposite the supermarket.
- Is it near here?
- Yes, it's between the bank and the café. Thank you!

⚠️ More common mistakes
1. Using "to" for position: The dog is to the garden → in the garden.
2. Mixing "behind" and "in front of".
3. Forgetting the article "the": on table → on the table.

⭐ Recap
- Prepositions of place answer the question "Where?".
- in = inside, on = on a surface, under = below.
- behind, in front of, next to, between, near, opposite for wider positions.
- Use them with "to be" and with "there is / there are".
- "between" needs two things; "in front of" and "next to" need the small words "of" and "to".

📘 Language bank
Prepositions: in, on, under, behind, in front of, next to, beside, between, near, opposite, above, below.
Places: table, chair, bed, wall, door, window, box, shelf, garden, school, bank, shop.
Useful sentences: The book is on the desk. / My bag is under the chair. / The school is opposite the mosque. / Where is my phone? — It's next to the computer. / There are some pictures on the wall.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Choose the correct preposition.
1. The cat is (in / on / under) the table, sleeping on the floor beneath it.
2. There is a poster (in / on / behind) the wall.
3. The keys are (on / in / under) the drawer.
4. The school is (opposite / under / in) the mosque.
5. The bank is (between / on / in) the café and the shop.

Exercise 2 — Complete with the correct preposition.
1. My bag is ______ the chair. (below it)
2. The lamp is ______ the desk. (on top of it)
3. There is a mirror ______ the door. (at the back)
4. The plants are ______ ______ the window. (at the front)
5. Sit ______ ______ me, please. (at my side)

Exercise 3 — Answer the questions about your classroom.
1. Where is the board?
2. Where is your bag?
3. What is next to the door?

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: 1. under 2. on 3. in 4. opposite 5. between.
Exercise 2: 1. under 2. on 3. behind 4. in front of 5. next to.

🗣️ Speaking task
Play "Where is it?" with a partner. One student hides a small object (a pen, a rubber) and gives clues: "It is under something. It is next to the window." The other guesses the place using prepositions.

👀 Extra note
Three little words often get forgotten. Do not drop them:
- in front OF the house (not "in front the house").
- next TO the door (not "next the door").
- between the door AND the window (between always needs two things).
Getting these small words right makes your English sound natural.

🌍 Real-life English
Prepositions of place help you find things and give directions in real life. When you lose something, you use them: "My keys are on the table, in my bag, or under the sofa." When you help a visitor, you use them: "The pharmacy is next to the bank, opposite the school." Try describing the exact position of five objects in your room right now, then explain how to get from your classroom to the school gate using in front of, next to, opposite and between. These small words turn a vague idea into a clear picture that anyone can follow.

📋 Summary
- Prepositions of place answer the question "Where?" and always come before the place noun.
- in = inside something · on = touching a surface · under = below something.
- Wider positions: behind, in front of, next to/beside, between, near, opposite, above, below.
- "between" needs two things; "in front of" and "next to" need the small words "of" and "to" — don't drop them.
- Position sentences follow: subject + verb (is/are) + preposition + the + place, or "There is/are + preposition + place".
- Questions use "Where is/are + subject?" — is for singular, are for plural.
- Prepositions of place also describe directions in town: opposite the bank, next to the school, between the café and the shop.
- Common mistakes: confusing in/on, forgetting "of" or "to", forgetting the article "the".
